body_text:
For a predicate $P(x)$ on a domain $D$, the existential
statement $\exists x\in D\,P(x)$ (read *there exists $x$ in $D$
such that $P(x)$*) is true exactly when at least one element
$a\in D$ satisfies $P(a)$. Such an element is called a
*witness*.

An existential claim can be proved *constructively* by
explicitly producing a witness and verifying that it satisfies
$P$, or *non-constructively* by demonstrating that the
assumption that no witness exists leads to an insurmountable
contradiction. Note that an existential assertion guarantees
only that *at least one* witness exists; it makes no claim
regarding whether the witness is unique.
